Unit 1: Why Containers Exist

Learning objectives

Explain problems solved by containers.

Compare physical servers, virtual machines and containers.

Place containers in the DevOps lifecycle. Why this matters
Containers improve consistency, packaging and deployment speed by combining application code with its
declared runtime dependencies. Before containers
Applications often behaved differently across developer laptops, test systems and production because operating
systems, libraries, configuration and manual setup drifted. Containers versus virtual machines

Virtual machines emulate or virtualize hardware and usually run full guest operating systems.

Containers share the host kernel while isolating processes, filesystems, networks and resource views.

Containers are lighter, but they are not automatically more secure than virtual machines. DevOps flow
Source code -> image build -> automated tests -> registry -> deployment platform -> observability -> rollback
or promotion. How companies use this
Professional teams encode this practice in source-controlled standards, CI policies, image registries, automated
checks, least-privilege access and documented rollback. Common mistakes and prevention

Do not use production hosts for experiments.

Do not rely on mutable tags or undocumented manual changes.

Docker is easier to operate when containers are understood as Linux processes with isolation and resource

Learning objectives

EOF
